from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Primes are the fundamental atoms of arithmetic.",
            "They appear random, yet follow asymptotic patterns.",
            "Sieve of Eratosthenes filters integers.",
            "Primes become sparser as numbers grow.",
            "Order emerges from apparent chaotic distribution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Elusive Prime Patterns", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight primes in gold
        num_line = VGroup(*[Text(str(i), font_size=16) for i in range(1, 21)])
        num_line.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(num_line, 'B1', scale_factor=1.0)
        primes = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19]
        for i in primes:
            num_line[i-1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(num_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Sieve Animation
        sieve_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.4).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3) for _ in range(25)])
        sieve_grid.arrange_in_grid(rows=5, cols=5, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(sieve_grid, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(sieve_grid))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Density Graph
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 2], y_range=[0, 1, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'E3', scale_factor=0.4)
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 1/np.sqrt(x+1), color=WHITE)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF6347"), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Chaotic movement
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color=WHITE) for _ in range(10)])
        self.place_at_grid(dots, 'F4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF7F"), run_time=1)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[ApplyMethod(d.shift, np.array([0.5*np.random.randn(), 0.5*np.random.randn(), 0])) for d in dots]))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Primes bridge the discrete to the continuous.",
            "The Euler Product Formula connects primes to Pi.",
            "Reciprocals of prime squares converge.",
            "Infinite products reveal circular geometry.",
            "Robot arm draws a perfect circle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Approximating Pi via Prime Logic", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)

        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        formula = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \prod_{p} \frac{1}{1-p^{-s}}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Representing sum of 1/p^2
        sum_text = MathTex(r"\sum \frac{1}{p^2} \approx 0.452", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_text, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05) for _ in range(20)])
        dots.arrange_in_grid(4, 5, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(dots, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        arm = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(arm, 'F3')
        self.play(Rotate(arm, angle=2*PI, about_point=arm.get_start()))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF4500")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Dirichlet's Theorem explores primes in arithmetic progressions.",
            "Primes of form a + nd exist infinitely.",
            "Numbers sorted into columns by remainder.",
            "Prime-filled columns extend infinitely.",
            "Primes never run out of destinations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Dirichlet's Theorem on Arithmetic Progressions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup (Numbers 0-23, arranged in 4 columns for mod 4)
        numbers = VGroup(*[Text(str(i), font_size=20) for i in range(24)])
        grid_visual = VGroup(*[numbers[i:i+6] for i in range(0, 24, 6)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(grid_visual, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#4682B4"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        # Highlight columns representing arithmetic progressions (e.g., 1+4n)
        progression = VGroup(grid_visual[0][1], grid_visual[1][1], grid_visual[2][1], grid_visual[3][1])
        self.play(progression.animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        # Animate markers moving (representing drone/primes)
        dot = Dot(color="#32CD32").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "A2")
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(self.grid["F2"]), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Flash intersection points
        flash = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#32CD32").move_to(dot.get_center())
        self.play(Flash(dot.get_center(), color="#32CD32", line_length=0.3, num_lines=8))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Conclusion", [
            "Primes hide deep structural order within chaos.",
            "Arithmetic links the discrete to Pi.",
            "[Asset: FinalMosaic] Beautiful order emerges from perceived randomness."
        ])
        
        # Representations (random dots that will form a pattern)
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(50)])
        for d in dots:
            d.move_to(self.grid["C3"] + np.random.uniform(-1, 1, 3))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(dots.animate.arrange_in_grid(rows=5, cols=10, buff=0.1).scale(0.5).move_to(self.grid["C3"]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Using placeholder for the mosaic since asset file path isn't real
        mosaic_placeholder = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#FFD700").move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(dots, mosaic_placeholder))
        self.play(Indicate(mosaic_placeholder))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture[0], self.lecture[1], self.lecture[2], mosaic_placeholder, self.title))

outline.topic: The Hidden Order of Numbers: Primes, Pi, and Dirichlet
outline.target_audience: University students with a foundational interest in Number Theory

sections.title: The Elusive Prime Patterns
sections.content: Introduce prime numbers as the 'atoms' of arithmetic. Explain the challenge of prime distribution—they appear random, yet follow asymptotic patterns like the Prime Number Theorem. Use a visual 'Sieve of Eratosthenes' animation that fades into a density graph to show how primes become sparser as numbers grow.
sections.example: Imagine a flock of starlings (primes) moving across a field; while individual movements seem chaotic, the entire flock moves with a predictable density structure.

sections.title: Approximating Pi via Prime Logic
sections.content: Connect the discrete world of primes to the continuous world of Pi. Introduce the Euler Product Formula: ζ(s) = Π(1-p^-s)^-1. Visualize this by showing how the infinite product of prime-based terms converges to values involving Pi (e.g., the Basel problem).
sections.example: A robotic arm attempting to draw a perfect circle; if the arm adjusts its precision based on the reciprocal of prime squares, it converges exactly to the geometry of Pi.

sections.title: Dirichlet's Theorem on Arithmetic Progressions
sections.content: Introduce the prerequisite: modular arithmetic. Dirichlet’s Theorem states that for any two coprime integers a and d, there are infinitely many primes of the form a + nd. Use a color-coded grid animation where numbers are sorted into columns by their remainders; highlight that 'prime-filled' columns extend infinitely.
sections.example: A delivery drone (the prime number) is restricted to fly only on specific streets (arithmetic progressions) that don't share a common hub with the city center (coprime to d). Dirichlet proves the drone never runs out of destinations.

sections.title: Synthesis and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize the bridge between the 'random' distribution of primes and their deep structural ties to Pi and arithmetic progression. Reinforce that mathematical beauty lies in finding order within perceived chaos.
sections.example: A mosaic artist (the mathematician) placing tiles—each tile (prime) seems randomly chosen, yet when zoomed out, the entire floor forms a perfectly circular pattern (Pi).
